text: Entropy as a measure of uncertainty.
expected_response: Entropy quantifies the average uncertainty or surprise in a random variable. Higher entropy means outcomes are more unpredictable, while lower entropy means the distribution is more concentrated and predictable.

Mutual information measures how much knowing one variable reduces uncertainty about another. It captures all forms of statistical dependence, not just linear correlation, and is zero only when the variables are completely independent.

KL divergence measures how one probability distribution differs from another reference distribution. It quantifies the inefficiency of assuming distribution Q when the true distribution is P, and is always non-negative but asymmetric.

text: Channel capacity of a noisy communication channel.
expected_response: Channel capacity is the maximum rate at which information can be transmitted over a noisy channel with arbitrarily low error. It depends on the channel's noise characteristics and is achieved by optimizing input distributions.

Shannon's source coding theorem states that no lossless compression scheme can reduce the average code length below the entropy of the source. It establishes entropy as the fundamental limit of compression.

Fano's inequality provides a lower bound on the probability of classification error in terms of conditional entropy. It links uncertainty about the true label to the minimum achievable error of any decoder.

The data processing inequality states that processing data cannot increase the mutual information between variables. Once information is lost through a transformation, no further processing can recover it.

Cross-entropy measures the expected number of bits needed to encode samples from a true distribution P using a code optimized for Q. In machine learning, it penalizes models that assign low probability to the correct class.

Rate-distortion theory characterizes the minimum number of bits per symbol needed to encode data while allowing a specified level of distortion. It formalizes the tradeoff between compression rate and reconstruction quality.

Fisher information measures how sensitive a probability distribution is to changes in an underlying parameter. Higher Fisher information means the parameter can be estimated more precisely from observed data.

text: Differential entropy for continuous random variables.
expected_response: Entropy for continuous variables is called differential entropy; it measures uncertainty in a distribution via its density. Unlike discrete entropy, it can be negative because it depends on the choice of coordinates, but differences in differential entropy still meaningfully compare uncertainty between densities on a common scale.

Conditional entropy quantifies the remaining uncertainty in a random variable X after observing another variable Y. It measures how unpredictable X is when Y is known, and it becomes zero when X is fully determined by Y.

text: Joint entropy of two random variables.
expected_response: Joint entropy measures the total uncertainty in a pair of random variables considered together. It reflects both their individual unpredictability and the structure of their dependence.

Jensen-Shannon divergence symmetrizes KL divergence by averaging the two distributions and measuring how far each is from their mixture. It is always finite and symmetric; its square root yields the Jensen-Shannon distance, which is a true metric.
Total variation distance measures the maximum difference in probability assigned by two distributions over all events. It captures how distinguishable the distributions are from one another.

Hellinger distance quantifies similarity between two probability distributions using the square roots of their densities. It is symmetric, bounded between 0 and 1, and is useful in statistical inference.

Huffman coding builds an optimal prefix-free code for a given distribution by assigning shorter codewords to more probable symbols. It minimizes expected code length among all binary prefix codes for that source.

Arithmetic coding encodes an entire message as a subinterval of [0, 1), refining the interval symbol by symbol. With long messages it can approach entropy rate more tightly than symbol-wise Huffman coding, especially for skewed or complex sources.

text: Universal coding without a fixed source model.
expected_response: Universal coding refers to compression schemes that do not assume prior knowledge of the source distribution. They adaptively learn structure from data and, for broad source classes, achieve average lengths close to the source's entropy rate.

A binary symmetric channel flips each transmitted bit independently with a fixed crossover probability. It is a canonical noisy channel model used to develop intuition for error probability and error-correcting codes.

The AWGN channel models communication where the received signal equals the transmitted signal plus Gaussian noise. It is widely used in digital communication theory and has a well-known capacity formula under power constraints.

Error-correcting codes add structured redundancy so the receiver can detect and correct errors caused by channel noise. Well-chosen codes enable reliable communication at rates approaching channel capacity.

The Cramer-Rao bound gives a lower limit on the variance of unbiased estimators of a parameter. It shows that Fisher information constrains how precisely a parameter can be estimated from data under regularity conditions.

The MDL principle prefers explanations that minimize the total codelength of the model plus the encoded data given that model. It links statistical model selection to compression: simpler models that still fit the data well are favored.

The information bottleneck learns a representation of an input variable that retains information about a target variable while compressing irrelevant detail. It formalizes the tradeoff between compression of the input and retained predictive information about the target.

text: Entropy of a discrete random variable.
expected_response: Entropy measures the average uncertainty in a discrete random variable. It is largest when outcomes are close to uniformly distributed and smallest when probability concentrates on a single outcome.

Differential entropy extends entropy to continuous distributions. Individual values can be negative because they depend on scaling, but differences of differential entropies still quantify relative uncertainty in a consistent way.

text: Joint entropy of two random variables.
expected_response: Joint entropy quantifies the total uncertainty in a pair of variables taken together, beyond what either margin alone expresses.

text: Conditional entropy after observing another variable.
expected_response: Conditional entropy measures how much uncertainty remains in X after observing Y. It vanishes when X is a deterministic function of Y.

text: Entropy rate of a stationary stochastic process.
expected_response: The entropy rate of a stochastic process is the per-symbol uncertainty in the limit for long sequences. For stationary processes it captures the irreducible randomness per time step generated by the source.
Mutual information measures how much knowing one variable reduces uncertainty about another. Unlike correlation, it detects arbitrary statistical dependence, not only linear relationships.
Conditional mutual information quantifies the dependence between two variables after conditioning on a third. It isolates how much association remains when common causes shared with Z are removed.

Multi-information generalizes pairwise mutual information to several variables by measuring how much their joint distribution departs from full independence. It summarizes shared stochastic structure across the whole set.
Interaction information describes how three or more variables share information beyond pairwise terms. It can reveal synergistic or redundant components of multivariate dependence.
KL divergence measures how one distribution P differs from a reference Q. It is nonnegative, asymmetric, and is infinite when Q assigns zero mass where P does not.

text: Jensen-Shannon divergence as a symmetric divergence.
expected_response: Jensen-Shannon divergence smooths KL divergence toward a mixture of the two arguments, yielding a symmetric, finite quantity. Its square root is a metric on probability distributions.
Total variation distance equals the largest gap between the probabilities the two laws assign to any event. It directly controls the optimal error of hypothesis tests between them.

text: Hellinger distance via density square roots.
expected_response: The Hellinger distance compares square roots of densities, producing a bounded, symmetric measure of similarity. It relates to affinity measures used in hypothesis testing and density estimation.

Renyi divergence parametrizes a family of divergences that interpolate between different emphasis on tail mass. It generalizes KL divergence in the limit and is useful in robust statistics and hypothesis testing.
The source coding theorem states that lossless compression cannot beat the entropy rate on average. Codes can approach entropy from above, but not below, for ergodic sources in the large-block limit.

text: Huffman coding and optimal prefix codes.
expected_response: Huffman's algorithm builds a prefix-free code minimizing expected length for a given symbol distribution. It is optimal among memoryless symbol-by-symbol binary prefix codes.

Arithmetic coding maps long sequences to nested subintervals of the unit interval, letting per-symbol codelengths track fractional bit costs. For long messages it can approach entropy more closely than Huffman in many practical settings.
Lempel-Ziv schemes parse the stream into repeated phrases and grow an adaptive dictionary online. They need no prior model of the source and are universal for broad ergodic classes.
Universal codes adapt probabilities from the data and achieve compressed lengths close to the entropy rate without knowing the law in advance, under mild assumptions on the source class.

text: Binary symmetric channel with crossover probability.
expected_response: The BSC independently flips bits with some probability p. It is a minimal model of symmetric noise used to study code rates and decoding error exponents.

The binary erasure channel delivers the bit correctly or replaces it with an erasure symbol the receiver knows is unknown. It cleanly separates lost bits from corrupted bits and is analytically tractable.
An AWGN channel adds zero-mean Gaussian noise with flat spectrum to the transmitted waveform. It underpins many capacity results in continuous-time and discrete-time communication.

text: Channel capacity and maximum reliable rate.
expected_response: Channel capacity is the supremum of rates at which there exist codes making error probability arbitrarily small. It captures the intrinsic information-carrying ability of the noisy channel.

text: Shannon-Hartley theorem for bandlimited Gaussian channels.
expected_response: The Shannon-Hartley theorem gives the capacity of a band-limited AWGN channel: it grows with bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio, linking physics constraints to maximum error-free data rate.
Error-correcting codes embed parity and structure so noise-induced transitions stay within correctable regions of the codeword space. They translate channel capacity into practical reliability.
Linear block codes represent messages as vectors in a linear subspace over a finite field. Their algebraic structure enables efficient encoding and syndrome-based decoding.
Convolutional codes shift registers convolve incoming bits with fixed taps, spreading memory across time. Decoders use trellises or similar structures to approximate maximum-likelihood sequences.
Turbo codes parallel-concatenate component convolutional codes with interleaving and iterate soft decoding between them. They brought practical performance very close to Shannon limits.
LDPC codes use sparse bipartite graphs of variable and check nodes. Iterative belief-propagation decoders exploit the sparsity for near-capacity performance with manageable complexity.
Fisher information scores how much small parameter changes tilt the likelihood. Larger curvature implies sharper likelihood peaks and, via the Cramer-Rao bound, tighter estimation limits.
The Cramer-Rao inequality lower-bounds the variance of unbiased estimators using Fisher information. No unbiased procedure can beat this bound under standard regularity assumptions.
MDL formalizes Occam's razor by scoring models with the bits needed to describe both the hypothesis and the data it compresses, balancing fit and complexity.

The information bottleneck optimizes a representation that throws away information about the input except what helps predict a target. It yields Pareto-optimal points between compression and prediction.
Rate-distortion theory maps allowable distortion levels to minimum representation rates for a source. It extends lossless coding to lossy compression with principled trade curves.
Kolmogorov complexity is the length of the shortest program on a fixed universal machine that outputs a string. It formalizes algorithmic randomness and is only computable up to an additive constant.
Algorithmic mutual information compares the independent descriptions of two strings with the joint shortest description, capturing shared compressible structure at the bit level.
A statistic is sufficient for a parameter if the data's conditional law given the statistic does not depend on that parameter. It captures all Fisher information about the parameter in the sample.
Typical sets contain sequences whose empirical entropies match the source law. Most long draws concentrate there, letting us count sequences and prove coding theorems.

The asymptotic equipartition property says that for many sources (e.g., i.i.d.), long sequences concentrate on a typical set where each sequence has roughly the same probability, on the order of 2 raised to the power (-n times the entropy H), and the normalized log-probability converges to the entropy rate. It underpins proofs of source and channel coding theorems.
